##Overview

This application implements two market area models, namely: Multiplicative Competitive Interaction Model and Huff Model.


###Loading the R library

```{r}
library(MCI)
library(dplyr)
```

##Interactive Matrix

A spatial interaction is a realized movement of people, freight or information between an origin and a destination.  It is a transport demand / supply relationship expressed over a geographical space.  

In this section, you will build a simple spatial interactive matrix by compbining a distance matrix (Subzone_Distance.csv) and a market area file (e.g. Subzone_Pop_2013.csv).

The read.csv function of R will be used to import these two data files into R environment.

First, we will import the distance matrix file.

```{r}
Distance_Matrix <- read.csv("D:/Library Analytics/MCI/dataTest/Subzone_Distance.csv")
```

Next, we will import the library information file.

```{r}
POI_Info <- read.csv("D:/Library Analytics/MCI/dataTest/Lib_Info_13.csv")
```

Create dummy variables for library types
```{r}
POI_Info <- transform(POI_Info, type_if_mall = ifelse(Branch.Type == "Mall",1,0))
POI_Info <- transform(POI_Info, type_if_standalone = ifelse(Branch.Type == "Stand-Alone",1,0))
```

Now, we are going to use the left.join function of dplyr to combine the Distance_Matrix and POI_INFO using 

```{r}
Interactive_Matrix <- left_join(Distance_Matrix, POI_Info)
```

###A simple MCI model

We can test the completeness of the interactive matrix created by building a simple Huff model.

```{r}
MCI_mat <- mci.shares(Interactive_Matrix, "Subzone", "Branch", "Collection.Size",1,"Distance_km",-2)
```

```{r}
mci_model <- mci.fit(MCI_mat, "Subzone", "Branch", "p_ij","Distance_km", "Branch.Gross.Floor.Area","Collection.Size","No..of.Tuition.Centres.Within.1KM","type_if_mall", "type_if_standalone")
summary(mci_model)
```

## MCI Model using Transaction Data

###Import patrons' transaction data 

Read library patrons' transaction data into R environment
```{r}
Transaction_Data <- read.csv("D:/Library Analytics/MCI/dataTest/TXN_FY13_data.csv")
```

Removing the transactions where uid = 0 (unidentified)
```{r}
Transaction_Data <- Transaction_Data[(Transaction_Data$Patron.UID != 0),]
```

###Import Patron Data
```{r}
Patron_Data <- read.csv("D:/Library Analytics/MCI/dataTest/Patron_Dataset_FY13_Subzone.csv")
```

Remove "Bad Value" & "Missing Value" under Locale Planning ADZID
```{r}
Patron_Data <- Patron_Data[(Patron_Data$Locale.Planning.ADZID != "Bad Value")&
                                                             (Patron_Data$Locale.Planning.ADZID != "Missing Value"),]
```

Adding patrons' information
```{r}
Transaction_Data1 <- merge(Transaction_Data, Patron_Data, by.x="Patron.UID", by.y="Patron.UID", all.x = TRUE)
```

###Cleaning Patron Data

We found several data quality issues in the patron data.  Below are codes used to clean the patron data.

Patron_Data1 <- Patron_Data1[(Patron_Data1$Patron.Birthyear != 1900),]
Patron_Data1 <- merge(Patron_Data1, MA, by.x="Subzone", by.y="Subzone", all.x = TRUE)
Patron_Data2 <- Patron_Data1[(Patron_Data1$Subzone !="CKSZ07"),]


### Loading Market Area Data
A market area is a geographic zone containing the people who are likely to purchase a firm's goods or services.

Load location data (e.g. subzone) and their corresponding attrbiutes into R environment

```{r}
MA <- read.csv("D:/Library Analytics/MCI/dataTest/Subzone_Pop_2013.csv")[ ,c('Subzone', 'Population')]
```

###Import POI_Data

```{r}
POI_Data <- read.csv("D:/Library Analytics/MCI/dataTest/Lib_Data_13.csv")
```

Fitting MCI model

```{r}
mci_model <- mci.fit(ijmatrix, "Subzone.x", "Branch", "p_ij_obs","Distance_km", "Branch.Gross.Floor.Area","Collection.Size","No..of.Tuition.Centres.Within.1KM","type_if_mall", "type_if_standalone")
summary(mci_model)
```



#Interaction matrix

###Create an Interaction Matrix
Creates an interaction matrix based on the observed frequencies (automatically) market shares are corrected when they do not match the MCI standards (pij = 0) by adding absolute value 0.1

```{r}
ijmatrix_TXN_FY13 <- ijmatrix.create(Transaction_Data, "Subzone","Branch.Code", correctVar = TRUE, correctVar.val = 1)
```

ijmatrix <- merge(ijmatrix_TXN_FY13, Interactive_Matrix, by.x="interaction", by.y="route", all.x = TRUE)






###Preparing Interaction Matrix

library(xlsx)
write.xlsx(Patron_Data1, "F:/nlb/dataTest/Patron_Data1.xlsx")

###Adding the distance matrix 

Adding the distances from each subzone to library
```{r}
ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist <- merge(ijmatrix_TXN_FY13, Distance_Matrix, by.x="interaction", by.y="route", all.x = TRUE)
```

### delete duplicate columns
```{r}
ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist$from_Subzone <- NULL
ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist$to_Branch.Code <- NULL
```

###Removing invalid records 
Removing the rows where no distance is available CKSZ07 is not a valid subzone code from the 2014 shape file extracted from data.gov.sg. So the corresponding transaction records should be double-checked with NLB.

```{r}
ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist_rect <- ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist[!is.na(ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist$Distance_km),]
```

test1 <- ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist[is.na(ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist$Distance_km),]

Merge various dataset to get the attractiveness value ready
Include population information

```{r}
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data <- merge(ijmatrix_TXNFY13_dist_rect, MA, by.x="Subzone", by.y="Subzone", all.x = TRUE)
```

Include library information
```{r}
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data <- merge(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data, POI_Info, by.x="Branch.Code", by.y="Branch.Code", all.x = TRUE)
```

Correct values by adding 0.01 to elimate 0, otherwise the variables cannot be passed in mci.transmat function
```{r}
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$No..of.MRT.Within.1KM <- ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$No..of.MRT.Within.1KM + 0.01
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$No..of.Malls.Within.1KM <- ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$No..of.Malls.Within.1KM + 0.01
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$No..of.Tuition.Centres.Within.1KM <- ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$No..of.Tuition.Centres.Within.1KM + 0.01
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$Population <- ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$Population + 0.01
```

###Log-centering transformation of the interaction matrix

```{r}
ijmatrix_TXN13_transf <- mci.transmat(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data, "Subzone","Branch.Code","p_ij_obs","Distance_km", "Branch.Gross.Floor.Area", "Collection.Size", "type_if_mall","type_if_standalone","Population", "No..of.MRT.Within.1KM","No..of.Malls.Within.1KM", "No..of.Tuition.Centres.Within.1KM")
```

#Plotting Model output

Plot variable Population to see the distribution before & after transformation Before mci.transmat

d <- density(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$Population)
plot(d, type="n", main="Population")
polygon(d, col="lightgray", border="lightgray")

After mci.transmat
d_t <- density(ijmatrix_TXN13_transf$Population_t)
plot(d_t, type="n", main="Population")
polygon(d_t, col="lightgray", border="lightgray")

Test to see if the transformation generates any zero/negative value
test <- ijmatrix_TXN13_transf[(ijmatrix_TXN13_transf$Population_t <= 0),] - TRUE!!!

However, zero/negative values are invalid in MCI model due to the impossibility of negative market share

```{r}
mcimodel_lib_patronage <- mci.fit(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data,"Subzone","Branch.Code", "p_ij_obs", "Distance_km", "Branch.Gross.Floor.Area", "Collection.Size","type_if_mall","type_if_standalone","Population", "No..of.MRT.Within.1KM","No..of.Malls.Within.1KM", "No..of.Tuition.Centres.Within.1KM")

# to add the predicted composite value to the data, for huff model
```{r}
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$predicted_value <- predict.lm(mcimodel_lib_patronage)
```

{ Huff Model: huff.fit function }
{huff.fit}
This function fits the Huff model with a given interaction matrix by optimizing the attractivity values of suppliers/locations iteratively and calculates the market shares/market areas

This code need to check:

huff_fit_total <- huff.fit(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data, "Subzone", "Branch.Code", "predicted_value", "Distance_km", lambda = -2, dtype= "pow", lambda2 = NULL, MA, "Subzone", "Population", POI_Data, "Branch.Code", "Number.of.Books.Borrowed", tolerance = 1, iterations = 2, output = "matrix", show_proc = TRUE)
```

Eliminate all negative/zero value in the data and run huff.fit again 
```{r}
ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data_positive <- ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data[(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data$predicted_value > 0),]
```

#Codes need to be validation

huff_fit_total_corr <- huff.fit(ijmatrix_Full_Txn_Data_positive, "Subzone", "Branch.Code", "predicted_value", "Distance_km", lambda = -2, dtype= "pow", lambda2 = NULL, Subzone_Pop_simple, "Subzone", "Population", Lib_Data, "Branch.Code", "Number.of.Books.Borrowed", tolerance = 1, iterations = 2, output = "matrix", show_proc = TRUE)

# PROBLEMS:
1. "CKSZ07" is not a valid subzone code from the "Master Plan 2014 Subzone Boundary (Web)" shape file extracted from data.gov.sg. So the corresponding transaction records should be double-checked and verified with NLB

2. For the subzones with population = 0 in year 2013 (data extracted from Statistics Singapore), there are, however, frequency more than 0, meaning there are people from those subzones visiting libraries, which doesn't make sense (e.g. subzone CHSZ03)

3. mci.transmat function generates zero/negative values for all numerical variables (excluding dummy ones), so the purpose of this step is unclear because the transformed output data frame "ijmatrix_TXN13_transf" is never used in any further step and yet, the variables in mci summary all have the "_t" in their names indicating they are after-transformation (?)

4. In the huff.fit function, the "lambda" represents a single numeric value for the (exponential) weighting of distance (transport costs0, so shall we replace the default -2 with the weightage of Distance_km we got from MCI summary -1.71 ?

5. Due to the existing of negative value in variable "predicated_value", huff.fit function runs with error immediately. (NA does not exist in the whole data frame)

6. Even all columns contain only positive values, huff.fit still cannot run successfully
